newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Cultus shares streak to record high.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Cultus shares streak to record high.

text.p: Shares in oil and gas explorer Cultus Petroleum NL bucked a weaker market trend on Friday to jump to a record high of A$2.86 as traders bought in on the back of an optimistic outlook on its exploration programme.
Brokers said the company had received promising results so far with more expected and this, rather than its softer first half net profit of A$3.43 million, had driven the interest.
"They have a good exploration book, particularly in the Otway Basin," said a Sydney-based dealer.
On February 28, the company said it had found a small quantity of oil in the Skull Creek West No 1 well in the Otway Basin and has since reported other gas shows in other wells in the permit area.
Others traders echoed similar sentiments, adding that the stock had been one of the best performers of the local market in the last 12 months.
"It's been a tremendous success story over the year, rising from the mid-50 cent range to these levels," said a Brisbane broker.
In 1997 alone, the stock has risen more than threefold from 91.1 cents to today's heady levels.
By 1.15 p.m. (0215 GMT), Cultus shares were 18 cents higher at A$2.77 on turnover of 839,461 shares.
